title: Lodeminting Review 2026: Is It Regulated or a Red Flag?
description: Is Lodeminting legit? We break down the 250 minimum deposit, the 2.9% card fee its FAQ lists and what its pages say about brokers and licences.
author: James Whitmore
content:
Lodeminting describes itself as an advanced technology platform that connects traders with licensed brokers and trades crypto automatically with AI. Its home page promises a low entry point, 24/7 support and withdrawals at any time, but names no operator and no regulator.

This review summarises what the Lodeminting site says about its method, costs, payments and support, shows where its own pages contradict each other, and lists the checks to run before you register.

Lodeminting Explained: What the Site Describes

According to its site, Lodeminting is an AI crypto trading platform that scans more than 100 signals per second and trades automatically, with a manual mode you can switch to. The footer adds that it connects traders with licensed brokers, selected automatically from a partner network.

The Conditions of Use describe the site as providing information about third-party platforms, and the contacts page repeats that it connects traders with licensed brokers. The site does not claim to be a broker itself.

Platform Overview

Category Description

Payment Methods Visa and Mastercard, bank transfer (SEPA, SWIFT), PayPal, crypto deposits (BTC, ETH, USDT)

Operator No company name, address or registration number given

Everything in this table is what the site states. We have not tested any of it and could not confirm it independently.

Lodeminting: Where It Delivers, Where It Doesn’t

Fair reviews cut both ways. Here is what the site offers, and what does not add up.

Lodeminting strengths, per its site:

  • No registration or subscription fee is stated.
  • Bank transfer and crypto deposits are listed at 0%, with deposits said to arrive in under 10 minutes.
  • Crypto withdrawals are described as usually finishing in under 30 minutes.
  • Two-factor authentication and real-time login alerts are mentioned.
  • The footer tells users to verify the licence of the broker they are matched with.

Where Lodeminting Falls Short:

  • No operator, regulator, licence number or registration number is named.
  • The home page says there are no hidden fees, while the FAQ lists a 2.9% fee on card payments.
  • The share of assets held offline is 98% on one page and 95% on another.
  • The FAQ regulator list reads like an unfilled template, and one FAQ item is an empty placeholder.
  • Performance claims such as 85% accuracy and returns of 18% to 31% come with no method or audit.

A polished page with large numbers is not a credential. Judge Lodeminting on the details it can back up, not on the figures it advertises.

What Actually Happens Behind Lodeminting

The site says its AI analyses markets continuously and places trades automatically, and that the system uses established algorithms to match you with a broker from its partner network. Trades are therefore not described as being run by Lodeminting itself.

The customer support section adds that all enquiries about your account should go to your partner broker directly, and that Lodeminting will only try to help resolve issues with that broker. Who the broker is, and who holds your money, is not stated.

None of this describes a method that can be checked, so treat the automation and the broker matching as claims, not as features we have confirmed.

Getting Set Up: What the Process Looks Like

This is the sign-up flow as the Lodeminting site describes it. We did not go through it ourselves.

1. Sign up

Create an account with your details. The FAQ says you pick your location at registration to see availability and local payment options.

2. Deposit funds

The offer is shown as from 250 by card or crypto. The FAQ adds that card deposits carry a 2.9% fee and that bank transfer and crypto deposits are at 0%.

3. Let the AI trade

Switch on automated trading, or use manual mode. The site then lists withdrawing at any time as the fourth step.

The home page shows a limited-time offer of 250 instead of 1000 with a countdown timer. Urgency like that is a sales device, not a reason to rush a deposit.

Breaking Down What Lodeminting Costs

The home page and the FAQ say there are no subscription fees, no registration costs and no hidden charges. The FAQ explains the lack of fees by saying revenue comes from premium features and volume-based exchange partnerships.

The FAQ payment list tells a different story for cards: Visa and Mastercard carry a 2.9% fee, while bank transfers and crypto deposits are at 0%. No trading spread, commission or withdrawal fee is described. Before you deposit, look for:

  • The 2.9% card fee, and whether it is charged again on withdrawal.
  • The spread or commission your partner broker applies on each trade.
  • Withdrawal fees and the minimum withdrawal amount.
  • Currency conversion charges, since the deposit currency is not stated.

The ROI calculator and the reported returns on the home page are illustrations. Treat them as marketing, not as a projection.

Which Assets Lodeminting Covers

The site lists cryptocurrencies, equities, forex, commodities, precious metals and CFDs, and mentions 65+ currencies. The FAQ says AI coin suggestions, ready-made portfolios and live buy and sell signals are available for top cryptocurrencies.

Because trades are said to run through partner brokers, which of these markets you can actually reach depends on the broker you are matched with. We could not confirm the list. Check inside your account before you rely on it:

  • Which assets you can really trade, and whether CFDs are offered to retail clients in your country.
  • The name and licence of the broker you are matched with.
  • Whether spreads and charges differ by asset.

Is Lodeminting Legit?

The site names no regulator, licence number or operating company. The footer only says the platform works with licensed brokers and tells users to verify the broker themselves. The Conditions of Use do not name the owner and describe the site as providing information about third-party platforms.

Several statements on the site do not line up:

  • No hidden fees on the home page, but a 2.9% card fee in the FAQ payment list.
  • 24/7 live chat and email support in the FAQ, but all account enquiries are sent to your partner broker.
  • 98% of assets stored offline on one page and 95% on another.
  • A 4.9 rating from 1,247 reviews in one block and 4.7 from 189 reviews in another.
  • Funds said to be insured against unauthorised access, with no insurer or amount named.
  • The FAQ regulator list is written in square brackets, which reads like an unfilled template.

If you are in Australia, businesses offering financial products to retail clients generally need an Australian Financial Services licence from ASIC. The Conditions cap liability in Australian dollars, but we could not confirm that Lodeminting holds a licence. Checks you can run yourself:

  • Search the company name and the matched broker on ASIC’s Financial Services Register.
  • Check ASIC’s investor alert list for the name and the website address.
  • Search the name on Scamwatch and MoneySmart for scam reports.
  • Check whether the broker belongs to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA).
  • Look up when the domain was registered, since a very new domain deserves extra care.

Legitimacy and profitability are different things. Even a licensed platform can lose you money if you overcommit or rely on best-case figures. This section is general information, not legal or financial advice.

Mistakes Worth Avoiding on Lodeminting

Most of the losses with automated trading tools trace back to user decisions, not the platform itself. A few worth flagging:

Assuming the name means the platform is established.

A memorable brand is not a substitute for checking the platform’s actual history and terms.

Funding well beyond the minimum right away.

Test the platform on your own terms before scaling up. That is exactly why a small first deposit makes sense.

Treating AI-assisted trading as fully hands-off.

Check your open positions regularly. Market conditions shift, and settings that worked last month may not fit now.

Ignoring fees and spreads.

Spreads, commissions and withdrawal charges all reduce what you keep, so note them before you deposit.

Skipping a small test withdrawal.

Payout terms are easy to overlook until you need them. Try a small withdrawal while the amount is still low.

A Quick Checklist Before Your First Live Trade

Run through this before committing real funds.

  • The broker you are matched with is named, and its licence is checked on the regulator’s own register.
  • Fees confirmed in writing, including the 2.9% card fee and any withdrawal fee.
  • Support route confirmed: who answers, Lodeminting or the broker.
  • Account verified, with a strong, unique password and two-factor authentication on.
  • First deposit kept to the 250 minimum, ignoring the countdown timer.
  • A small withdrawal tested early, before depositing more.
  • Performance claims treated as marketing until a method is shown.

Who Gets the Most Out of Lodeminting

Lodeminting may suit a newcomer who wants a low entry point of 250, will read the terms first and is prepared to identify and check the partner broker before depositing.

It is a poor fit for anyone who needs a named regulator and operator, who plans to rely on the advertised returns, or who wants an income they can leave on autopilot.

The platform underneath the claims is unconfirmed. Judge it on what you can check, not on the branding.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Lodeminting legit?

We could not confirm it. The site names no operator, regulator or licence number and says it only connects users to licensed brokers, so identify and check the broker before you deposit.

Is Lodeminting a scam?

We cannot say either way. Several statements on the site conflict with each other and no operator can be confirmed, so start small, test a withdrawal early and register only through the official website.

What is the Lodeminting minimum deposit?

From 250 by card or crypto, according to the site. The site does not state the currency, and the home page shows it as a limited-time offer.

Does Lodeminting charge fees?

The site says there are no subscription, registration or hidden fees, but the FAQ lists a 2.9% fee on Visa and Mastercard payments. No spread or withdrawal fee is described.

How long does a Lodeminting withdrawal take?

The FAQ says bank card withdrawals take 1 to 3 business days and crypto withdrawals usually finish in under 30 minutes, depending on your bank and verification status.

Is Lodeminting regulated?

No regulator is named. The site says it works with licensed brokers and asks users to verify the broker’s licence themselves.

Is Lodeminting a broker?

The site does not claim to be one. It says it connects traders with licensed brokers from a partner network and that account enquiries go to your broker.

Does Lodeminting have a mobile app?

No separate app is mentioned. The site describes multi-device compatibility in a browser.

What payment methods does Lodeminting accept?

Visa and Mastercard, bank transfer (SEPA and SWIFT), PayPal and crypto deposits in BTC, ETH and USDT are listed on the site.

Does Lodeminting guarantee profits?

No. The footer itself says all trading involves financial risk. Treat the 85% accuracy and the reported returns as marketing.

Where We Land on Lodeminting

Lodeminting offers a familiar AI-assisted pitch with a low 250 entry point and no registration fee, according to its own site. What it does not offer is a named operator, a named regulator or a consistent account of its own fees and support.

If you decide to try it, keep the first deposit small, find out which broker you are matched with and check its licence, and test a withdrawal before you add funds.
